sources.citation: Hauser & Bühlmann, Characterization and Greedy Learning of Interventional Markov Equivalence Classes of Directed Acyclic Graphs, JMLR 13 (2012)
Hauser & Bühlmann, Jointly interventional and observational data: estimation of interventional Markov equivalence classes of directed acyclic graphs

findings.finding: A fixed family of interventions generally refines observational Markov equivalence to an interventional equivalence class; it does not automatically identify a unique DAG.
findings.impact: A future H7 causal effect under frozen TOP1 cut supports the tested policy effect, not unique route topology. Broad topology claims require equivalence-class scope or additional identifying interventions.

sources.citation: He & Geng, Active Learning of Causal Networks with Intervention Experiments and Optimal Designs, JMLR 9 (2008)
Hauser & Bühlmann, Two Optimal Strategies for Active Learning of Causal Models from Interventional Data
Elahi et al., Adaptive Online Experimental Design for Causal Discovery, ICML 2024

findings.finding: Full structural recovery depends on intervention design. Separating systems and optimal intervention targets are used to orient ambiguities; more samples under a non-separating intervention family do not create structural information that the interventions never expose.
findings.impact: Any fresh H7 successor claiming unique route/edge structure should predeclare the graph features and demonstrate an adequate separating/identifying intervention design.

sources.citation: Yang, Katcoff & Uhler, Characterizing and Learning Equivalence Classes of Causal DAGs under Interventions, ICML 2018
Jaber et al., Causal Discovery from Soft Interventions with Unknown Targets, NeurIPS 2020
Zhang et al., Scalable Contrastive Causal Discovery under Unknown Soft Interventions (2026)

findings.finding: General/soft interventions and uncertain target semantics can preserve substantial structural equivalence even with interventional data.
findings.impact: H7 target selection is known but state-dependent. Fixed-target perfect-intervention identifiability results cannot be imported without treating the TOP1 selector, target map and actual intervention semantics as part of the causal object.

sources.citation: Gao et al., IDYNO: Learning Nonparametric DAGs from Interventional Dynamic Data, ICML 2022
Castri et al., CAnDOIT: Causal Discovery with Observational and Interventional Data from Time Series, Advanced Intelligent Systems (2024)

findings.finding: Interventional causal discovery in dynamical systems uses explicit temporal/lagged causal representations; a static DAG abstraction does not automatically capture recurrent feedback semantics.
findings.impact: Future H7 graph-identification claims should define an explicit time-unrolled/lagged causal object before invoking interventional-equivalence or topology-identification language.
